headlines.title: 4 Dividend Stocks Just Gave Shareholders a Raise. One Hiked Its Payout 17.5%
headlines.summary: A consulting firm, a student-loan servicer, a grocery-anchored REIT, and an oil giant all raised payouts in the same week. Each looks safe on paper, but every one carries a risk that could test the next increase.

headlines.title: COP Q3 2026 deep dive: capital discipline and portfolio efficiency offset production decline
headlines.summary: Oil and gas producer ConocoPhillips (NYSE:COP) reported revenue ahead of Wall Street’s expectations in Q3 2026, with sales up 29.2% year on year to $20.06 billion. Its non-GAAP profit of $3.27 per share was 7.3% above analysts’ consensus estimates.

headlines.title: Can ConocoPhillips Sustain Future Production Growth With Lower CapEx?
headlines.summary: COP plans modestly lower 2027 capital spending while growing production through low-cost resources and efficiency gains to strengthen long-term cash flow.

headlines.title: ConocoPhillips Trades at a Premium: Is It the Right Time to Buy?
headlines.summary: COP's 54.4% stock rally, low-cost assets, LNG expansion and Willow project fuel optimism, but its premium valuation raises concerns for investors.

description: ConocoPhillips explores for, produces, transports, and markets crude oil, bitumen, natural gas, liquefied natural gas (LNG), and natural gas liquids. It operates in five segments: Alaska; Lower 48; Canada; Europe, Middle East and North Africa; and Asia Pacific. The company's portfolio includes unconventional plays in North America; conventional assets in North America, Europe, Asia, and Australia; global LNG developments; oil sands assets in Canada; and an inventory of global exploration prospects. It serves in the United States, Canada, China, Equatorial Guinea, Libya, Malaysia, Norway, Singapore, the United Kingdom, and internationally. ConocoPhillips was founded in 1917 and is headquartered in Houston, Texas.
